summary: round 2, delta since 62e7a2e (spec as of 24c2847; docs/specs/CHG-0005 is unchanged from 62e7a2e to 24c2847 and from f1f0450 to HEAD): F-1, F-2, F-3, F-5, F-8 fixed. The SDD records Q14 (a) as decided at L50-L53, L115, L399 and L426-L431 and leaves no open question; it names corepack 0.34.0 in a build argument and in A11, adds the events block, adds the wrong-media-type smoke test cases, and adds host install steps plus Node for the smoke check. New: 2 minor (corepack auto-pin could change web/package.json on the host; a global npm install of corepack can collide with existing shims) and 1 info (0.34.0 could not be checked against npm here and is correctly an assumption). Carried unchanged: F-4, F-6 and F-7 (minor), F-9 to F-14 (info). Pass with 5 minor and 7 info follow-ups.

findings.message: The tests-first plan gives the test to the tests node and the script to the build node, but does not say who writes web/scripts/compose-smoke.d.mts, or whether the red commit carries a failing stub .mjs. Without the .d.mts, tsc --noEmit (pnpm typecheck and pnpm build) fails in the red commit for a missing module, not for the behaviour.
findings.suggestion: State that the React tests node writes compose-smoke.d.mts (signatures only) and a stub compose-smoke.mjs whose functions throw not implemented, and that the build node replaces the stub.

findings.message: Section 1 says that Section 6 below answers each section-9 question, but the answers are in section 4 (section 6 is Security and privacy).
The citation web/playwright.config.ts:L27-L29 for Chromium, Firefox and WebKit misses WebKit: L27 opens projects, and the three projects are L28-L30.

An error_log at emerg also drops alert-level lines (for example a worker process exiting on a signal), which carry no request data. Request-bearing lines are logged at crit and below, so alert would keep the privacy rule and lose less.
findings.suggestion: Consider error_log /dev/stdout alert, and update A10 and R6 to match.

findings.message: The jar and the SPA dist are platform-independent, yet both build stages run under emulation in the buildx proof, which is the slow part (R8).
findings.suggestion: Consider FROM --platform=BUILDPLATFORM (the BuildKit build argument) for both build stages so that only the run stages are per platform. Dockerfiles allow this; the no-dollar rule covers only docker-compose.yml.

findings.message: Neither .dockerignore excludes .env files. Vite reads a web/.env that a person made at build time, and an api/.env would enter the build stage. Neither reaches the run image, but excluding them is a cheap defence for NFR-102.
findings.suggestion: Add .env and .env.* (keeping .env.example) to api/.dockerignore and web/.dockerignore.

findings.message: The java module (api/) is listed as a plan module but gets no test. A java tests node therefore has no red commit to make, and the SDD does not say how that node is satisfied.
findings.suggestion: State what the java tests node delivers (nothing, a test-plan note, or that the plan has no java tests node) so plan extension does not stall.

findings.message: NFR-101, REQ-CMP-004 AC-1 and the no-query-string constraint are verified by inspection only. Cheap static Vitest checks (docker-compose.yml has no dollar sign and only 127.0.0.1 ports; the nginx log_format uses none of the request, args, query_string or http_referer variables) would turn them into regression tests.
findings.suggestion: Optional: add such checks in web/tests if the approver wants automated proof. The requirements do not require them.

findings.message: The base image tags pin only the major line (21-jdk-noble, 21-jre-noble, 26-slim) and rely on the P6 reading. Q11 as answered said major/minor tags. If the approver rejects P6 at freeze, the tags must change.
findings.suggestion: Mention in section 12 that the tags follow P6, and what they become if P6 is not confirmed.

findings.message: Corepack can write a packageManager field into a package.json that lacks one when it runs a package manager there (auto-pin, controlled by COREPACK_ENABLE_AUTO_PIN). The default in corepack 0.34.0 cannot be verified here, so the SDD should not depend on it. In the image a pin would touch only the build-stage copy. On the host, though, following 3.7 items 1 and 2 (corepack enable pnpm, then pnpm -C web install) could leave web/package.json modified. Section 2 says that file is not changed, and nothing records or checks the expectation.
findings.suggestion: Set COREPACK_ENABLE_AUTO_PIN=0 in the web build stage beside COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0. Add an assumption that the native README steps leave web/package.json unmodified, checked by git status after following them (U or I during build-node work). If the check fails, the README tells the person to export COREPACK_ENABLE_AUTO_PIN=0 before the native run.

findings.message: npm install -g corepack@0.34.0 may also install the shims corepack ships for pnpm and yarn, and npm can stop with EEXIST when such a bin already exists and npm does not own it. Examples: yarn 1 that official node images have placed in /usr/local/bin, a Homebrew or standalone pnpm, or shims left by an earlier corepack enable. This cannot be verified here. In the image, B would fail loudly. But L115 claims the step works on any Node, A7 says the npm install makes corepack present either way, and the host steps in 3.7 item 1 have no fallback or troubleshooting entry.
findings.suggestion: Mark the works-on-any-Node claim as an assumption checked by B. Name the fallback the build node may use if B fails on a bin conflict (for example npm install -g --force with the same pinned version). Add a README troubleshooting entry for EEXIST on the host step: remove the conflicting global pnpm or yarn, or use --force.

findings.message: corepack 0.34.0 is plausible (a 2025 release, after the npm signing-key rotation that broke older corepack releases), but it could not be checked against the npm registry here, and newer releases may exist by 2026-11. A11 correctly marks it as an assumption, and B fails if the version is not published or cannot activate pnpm 10.34.8.
findings.suggestion: Build node: record the corepack --version line from an uncached build log as A11 evidence. If the version is changed, change the build argument default and the README pin together.
